why: Builds the low, balanced stance everything else depends on.
say: Get low, feet wide, hands active — hold it, then slide on my point.
how: Spread out facing the coach.
Hold stance 15–20 seconds.
Coach points: slide 3 steps that way, back to center.

say: Watch the ball — slide where I point, backpedal when I pull, sprint on 'shot!'.
how: Rows of players in stance facing the coach.
Coach points left/right/back; players slide.
On 'shot!' everyone yells and sprints to box out.
h: Add closeouts on the coach's call.

why: Stops open shots without getting blown by.
say: Sprint at the shooter, chop your feet, one hand high — stay in front.
how: Defender under the rim passes to the wing.
Sprint two-thirds, chop steps the rest.
Offense makes one dribble move; defense contains.

say: Slide corner to corner, drop step, and keep your chest in front.
how: Lines on the baseline.
Slide in a zig-zag to half court (or full).
Jog back.

why: The foundation of team defense: positioning on every pass.
say: Every pass, everyone moves: on the ball, one pass away deny, two passes away help.
how: 4 offense on the perimeter, 4 defense.
Offense passes slowly; defense jumps to new spots on each pass.
Progress: add drives, then cuts, then live.
cue: Jump to the ball on the pass
e: Freeze after each pass; coach checks spots.

st: Pass — everyone jumps to new spots

why: Stopping the drive and getting back to your player.
say: Help stops the ball, then sprints back to their player on the pass.
how: 2 offense, 2 defense.
Ball handler drives; help defender stops the ball.
On the pass, help recovers with a closeout.
cue: Stop the ball outside the lane

why: Reaction and footwork without a ball.
say: Copy your partner — wherever they go, stay right in front.
how: Partners face each other.
Offense moves side to side; defense mirrors.
15 seconds, switch.

say: Pass, close out, keep them out of the middle — make them take a tough shot.
how: Defender passes to the wing and closes out.
Live 1v1, three dribbles max.
Offense to defense line, defense to the back.

why: Defending the most common action in basketball.
say: Screener's defender jumps out to slow the ball, then both recover.
how: 2-on-2 with a ball screen at the top.
Big's defender hedges out; guard's defender fights over.
Big recovers to the roller.

say: High side when the ball is up, low side when it goes to the corner.
how: Post on the block, passers on the wing and corner.
Defender plays 3/4 front on the high side.
Ball moves to the corner: step over to low side.

st: Ball to the corner — step over to low side
Back to the wing — high side

how: Pairs around the arc: defenders start in the lane with the ball.
Defender passes out and closes out.
Offense takes one hard dribble; defender contains.
Switch roles, then rotate one spot.

say: Defender, keep your chest in front and turn them. Ball handler, stay in your lane and try to get by.
how: Split the floor into lanes; one pair per lane.
Ball handler attacks down the lane; defender turns them as many times as possible.
Switch roles coming back.

var: Count the turns: three turns wins for the defense
Ball handler must use the weak hand

how: Three offense on the arc, three defenders in the lane, coach under the basket with the ball.
Coach passes to any offensive player.
Closest defender closes out; the others match up.
Play live to one shot. Defense must rebound to rotate off.
